nodes.name: From Jira
nodes.notes: Production URL: https://automation.sellux.ch/webhook/jira-<slug> - the only kind of path the login page lets through. Credential <slug>-jira-webhook (Header Auth: name X-NextUp-Jira, value a long random secret); the Jira automation rule sends the same header. Without the credential every call is refused.

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.notes: One copy of this workflow per company and Jira site. apiBase: the company's public address from automation.sellux.ch, http://app:3000 from an n8n inside its own stack. jiraBase: the Jira Cloud site, no trailing slash. jiraProject: the Jira project KEY. Rename the webhook path to jira-<slug> as well.

nodes.name: Poll or Jira?
nodes.notes: The schedule leads to the poll (NextUp -> Jira); the webhook, which carries a body, to Jira -> NextUp.

nodes.name: Read events
nodes.notes: Credential <slug>-nextup (Header Auth: Authorization = Bearer <token>). Needs events:read; the write-back nodes need events:write.

nodes.name: Jobs for Jira
nodes.notes: Active workflow only: the cursor stops before the first event that still needs Jira, so a failed epic or issue is tried again each minute, 5 times. After that, create it in Jira by hand. A manual run only lists what it would create.

nodes.name: Epic or issue?
nodes.notes: Epics run first (their branch is higher on the canvas), so a step added in the same minute as its project finds the epic.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ fields: { project: { key: $('Settings').first().json.jiraProject }, issuetype: { name: $('Settings').first().json.epicType }, summary: $json.title.slice(0, 250), description: { type: 'doc', version: 1, content: [{ type: 'paragraph', content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'Opened in NextUp (' + $json.slug + ') as project ' + $json.projectId + '. Its steps show up here as issues; moving one to Done moves the step in NextUp.' }] }] } } }) }}

nodes.name: Create epic
nodes.notes: Credential <slug>-jira (Basic Auth: the Atlassian account's e-mail + an API token from id.atlassian.com). Jira answers { id, key, self }.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ type: 'project.linked', target: $json.projectId, payload: { system: 'jira', key: $json.key, url: $json.url } }) }}

nodes.name: Link epic
nodes.notes: project.linked on the project. The app accepts it once project.linked is on the allow-list (SYSTEM_EVENT_TYPES); until then it answers 400. Continues on error, so the other items still run; a lost link can be added on the board by hand.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ fields: { project: { key: $('Settings').first().json.jiraProject }, issuetype: { name: $('Settings').first().json.stepType }, parent: { key: $json.epic }, summary: $json.text.slice(0, 250), description: { type: 'doc', version: 1, content: [{ type: 'paragraph', content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'A step of NextUp project ' + $json.projectId + ' (' + $json.slug + '). Move it to Done here and the step moves in NextUp.' }] }] } } }) }}

nodes.name: Create issue
nodes.notes: Same <slug>-jira credential. parent = the project's epic (works in team- and company-managed projects).

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ type: 'project.linked', target: $json.projectId, payload: { system: 'jira', key: $json.key, url: $json.url, stepId: $json.stepId } }) }}

nodes.name: Link issue
nodes.notes: project.linked with the stepId, so the board shows the issue on the step.

nodes.name: Read the status in Jira
nodes.notes: Same <slug>-jira credential. The status comes from Jira, never from the webhook body.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ type: 'project.step.moved', target: $json.projectId, payload: { stepId: $json.stepId, to: $json.to } }) }}

nodes.name: Move the step
nodes.notes: project.step.moved as system:n8n. Never project.done, measured, rewarded or stopped: people decide those.

nodes.name: Write the comment
nodes.notes: project.commented { text: 'Jira <KEY>: <comment>' } on the project, for a comment on the epic or on a step's issue.
